recurring_scale_anchors: 304×192 canvas; use one large primary cue and a small number of context cues so media concepts read at card size.
No readable words, captions, labels, logos, brands, letters or numerals; use blank bars, recognizable icons, imagery and device shapes only.
Differentiate public celebrity attention from online content creation, news reporting, and intrusive paparazzi photography.
Use a phone or screen only when it clarifies the media platform; avoid generic floating interface panels.
Keep people, cameras, paper folds and simple social icons large enough to read at card size.

polysemy_resolution_table.become a celebrity: A previously ordinary person steps into public fame, shown by a clear before-to-after change into a spotlight and public recognition.
polysemy_resolution_table.celebrity: A famous person recognized and warmly approached by fans; distinguish the individual from celebrity culture and press photographers.
polysemy_resolution_table.celebrity culture: A public fascination with famous people, shown as a crowd consuming celebrity images and news.
polysemy_resolution_table.influencer: An online creator makes a recommendation or demonstration directly to followers through a phone camera; not merely a famous actor.
polysemy_resolution_table.paparazzi: Professional photographers pursue a public figure for intrusive candid pictures, using long lenses and camera flashes.
polysemy_resolution_table.red carpet: A formal premiere arrival route lined with photographers and a featured guest; the carpet itself is the event cue.
polysemy_resolution_table.reality show: An unscripted participant is filmed during an ordinary real-life challenge; not a scripted drama.
polysemy_resolution_table.talent show: A performer demonstrates a skill on a competition stage before judges or an audience.
polysemy_resolution_table.opening night: The first public evening performance of a play, marked by a theater entrance, lit marquee shapes and an arriving audience.
polysemy_resolution_table.attention-grabbing: A striking image or headline visually catches a reader’s eye; no actual words are needed.
polysemy_resolution_table.exclusive interview: A one-to-one interview with a single reporter and invited subject in a private media setting; distinguish from a crowded press conference.
polysemy_resolution_table.headline news: A major current story singled out as the lead item in a broadcast or news feed.
polysemy_resolution_table.media: Different mass-communication channels together, such as newspaper, radio/microphone, television and digital screen; plural media, not a single medium.
polysemy_resolution_table.newspaper headline: The prominent top line area of a newspaper article, represented by blank bold bars and a related photo; no readable headline.
polysemy_resolution_table.sensationalize: A media outlet exaggerates a small event into a dramatic spectacle, shown by a modest event beside oversized alarmed coverage cues.
polysemy_resolution_table.article: A written newspaper or magazine piece with a clear topic photograph and structured columns.
polysemy_resolution_table.interview: A journalist asks a source questions and listens to an answer; media interview, not a job interview.
polysemy_resolution_table.news: A timely report of a real event, shown as factual coverage from a reporter or newsroom.
polysemy_resolution_table.newspaper: A folded or open broadsheet with multiple article columns and a photograph; distinguish from a bound book or magazine.
polysemy_resolution_table.photo: A printed or digital photograph being framed or viewed as a still image, distinct from a moving video.
polysemy_resolution_table.podcast: An episodic audio program recorded or heard through a microphone, headphones or player; not a music track alone.
polysemy_resolution_table.video: Moving visual footage displayed on a screen, distinct from a still photograph.
polysemy_resolution_table.website: A collection of linked web pages displayed in a browser window, with blank navigation and page sections; no brand or readable text.
polysemy_resolution_table.account: A personal social-media profile with an avatar and a few post tiles; not a bank or arithmetic account.
polysemy_resolution_table.comment: A viewer adds a response beneath a social post, represented by a speech bubble connected to a post tile.
polysemy_resolution_table.follow: A user subscribes to another person’s social-media updates, shown by tapping a person/profile connection icon.
polysemy_resolution_table.like: A user responds positively to a social-media post with a heart or thumbs-up reaction.
polysemy_resolution_table.post: A user publishes a photo or update to a social-media feed; not postal mail or a fence post.
polysemy_resolution_table.share: A user forwards or passes a social-media post to another person, shown by a connected share arrow.
polysemy_resolution_table.social media: A network of people and posts connected through digital profiles and phones.
polysemy_resolution_table.claim to fame: The particular achievement or feature for which someone is known, shown as one defining skill or accomplishment drawing public notice.
polysemy_resolution_table.exploit: A brave or remarkable achievement; use the lesson’s public-fame sense, not exploitation or abuse.
polysemy_resolution_table.expose: A journalist reveals a hidden fact or wrongdoing to public view, shown by uncovering a concealed document or evidence; not exposing skin.
polysemy_resolution_table.go to somebody’s head: New fame makes a person conceited, shown by a once-approachable person acting boastfully from an elevated position.
polysemy_resolution_table.have your name in lights: An aspiring performer sees their name represented by a blank star-shaped marquee sign lit above a theater; no letters or readable text.
polysemy_resolution_table.household name: A person so widely known that people of different ages in a home recognize the same face.
polysemy_resolution_table.in the public eye: A public figure is constantly visible to an audience, cameras and public attention.
polysemy_resolution_table.meteoric rise: A person’s fame increases very rapidly, shown by a sudden upward trajectory from small audience to a large spotlight/crowd.

glossary_context_notes: Lesson 67 groups celebrity attention, reporting and media formats, social-media actions, and fame expressions. Preserve those group senses when general glosses could point elsewhere.
Do not confuse a celebrity with an influencer; a news interview with a job interview; a social-media post with postal mail; or an achievement exploit with exploitation.
Keep adjacent lesson terms distinct: a red carpet is an event route, opening night is a first performance, talent show is a skills contest, and reality show is unscripted everyday footage.

existing_asset_triage.lesson_67: Reviewed exact-term same-name art from earlier lessons. Adapt only when the core medium or action directly matches; replace post office art and generic page spreads that do not read clearly as news media.

reviewed_candidates.reason: The open periodical spread already pairs a large topic photo with structured article columns; copy to Lesson 67 with the media-article key.
It clearly shows a reporter asking a guest questions with a camera recording; the television studio still fits the broader media-interview sense.
Two anchors at a broadcast desk with a world-news monitor clearly teach a timely news report.
The spread resembles a bound magazine or book and does not clearly read as a folded newspaper; create a recognizable broadsheet.
Microphone, headphones and an audio waveform make the podcast medium clear; reuse with the media-content key.
The browser-like frame and grouped page sections clearly teach a website; adapt to the lesson key.
A phone sends content to a physical mailbox, so postal delivery dominates; create an unmistakable social-feed post.
